disease_label_per_paper: Clostridium perfringens prosthetic joint infection following total knee arthroplasty
presentation_summary: A 64-year-old man underwent right total knee arthroplasty and then femoral-popliteal graft embolectomy 2 weeks later for critical limb ischemia.
Two weeks after embolectomy, he presented with acute severe right knee pain and swelling, tachycardia in the 110s, WBC 23.2 x10^9/L, and lactate 3.1 mmol/L.
Exam showed right knee erythema, edema, severe tenderness, and pain with movement.
Radiograph showed swelling and gas in the anterior knee soft tissue with prosthesis in normal position.

Emergency knee aspiration revealed grossly purulent fluid with 93,000 neutrophils/uL; he required urgent irrigation/debridement, repeat debridement, later prosthesis explantation, synovectomy, and antimicrobial spacer.

quality_warnings: Presentation-time ranking uses recent TKA, acute prosthetic knee inflammation, soft-tissue gas, synovial purulence, WBC, lactate, and source-control need. Culture species, later WBC/lactate normalization, and revision outcome are non-ranking.
